author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through the existing visit form, reached by its address alone. Corrections validate like booking, change that visit in place without adding another, and return to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit is opened, then the existing visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) renders with the `visit` model attribute prefilled with that visit's current date and description.

[REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when a POST to the same URL submits a non-blank description and a date later than today, then that visit is updated and the response redirects to the owner detail page.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a pet with one booked visit, when that visit is corrected, then the pet still has exactly one visit, carrying the corrected date and description.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a blank description or a date of today or earlier, when a correction is POSTed, then the form is redisplayed with the offending field in error and the stored visit is unchanged.
[REQ-VIS-003] edge case 3: given a visitId that does not belong to the named pet, when the correction form is opened or submitted, then the request is refused and no visit changes.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, still declined)
Any edit link or other visible entry point on the owner detail page (owner decision: reachable by URL alone; possible follow-up request)
Relaxing the future-date rule for corrections to past visits (recorded as an Open Question)
Adding a veterinarian, status, or other new field to a visit
notes: Docs written this dispatch: docs/prd.md (NG-5 row narrowed, Non-Goals preamble, REQ-VIS-003 narrative, Done-when, edge cases 3-4, two Open Questions), new docs/adr/2026-09-18-non-goal-visit-cancellation-only.md, status line of docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md. docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new non-goal ADR; that file is outside product-requirements-expert write scope. Open question recorded rather than decided: whether a past visit may be corrected to a past date; the narrow reading applies the booking rule (future date). Edge case 3 (visit not belonging to the pet is refused) is the narrow reading of 'updates that visit'; the refusal mechanism is the design expert's. The template's title/button wording for edit vs. create is left to design within REQ-LANG-002. No new vocabulary terms were introduced.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction follows the existing edit shape of PetController (optional path variable on the shared model-attribute method, bind onto the resolved persisted entity, save the owner so the change cascades); see system-design.md § Contracts invariants paragraph and § Persistence. The adjustment has three parts. (1) The shared @ModelAttribute("visit") method in VisitController takes an optional visitId path variable. When it is present, the method resolves the existing visit through owner -> pet -> new Pet lookup by visit identity and does NOT create or attach a new Visit. When it is absent, the method keeps today's create-and-attach behavior. Without this, the current method adds a blank Visit to the pet on every request, including the edit routes, and the cascade would persist a second visit. (2) The non-future-date rule moves onto Visit as a query taking the reference day (e.g. whether its date is later than a given day). Both the booking and correction handlers call it and map a false answer to the existing field error code typeMismatch.visitDate. Copying the check into a new handler would be a fresh rule in a controller, which architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog *Web controller* row and its checklist line forbid. (3) Pet gains a resolve-by-identity lookup for one of its visits, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). No new module, repository, or pattern. Basis: grep and file reads of VisitController, PetController, Pet, Owner, Visit (IDE oracle not connected; the weaker basis).
integration_points: Entry point GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit: renders pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with the resolved persisted Visit as model attribute `visit`, plus the existing `pet`, `owner`, and `minVisitDate` attributes. It binds nothing beyond path variables.

Entry point POST to the same URL: binding target is the resolved persisted Visit behind an allow-list of date and description (setAllowedFields). The existing disallow of id and *.id stays per security-principles.md mass-assignment row. The @InitBinder is shared, so booking binds through the same allow-list. On success it saves the owner and redirects to /owners/{ownerId} with a flash message. On error it redisplays the form without saving.

Refusal (edge case 3): a visitId absent from the named pet's visits is refused the same way VisitController already refuses a pet absent from the owner, by throwing IllegalArgumentException from the model-attribute method before any handler runs, so no save is reachable. Each request re-resolves owner, pet, and visit (security-principles.md, trusting cross-request state).
Double, framework transport: MockMvc via the existing @WebMvcTest(VisitController.class) slice, the sanctioned mock (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy).

Double, repository (OwnerRepository): the existing class-level @MockitoBean in VisitControllerTests, a conscious framework-stub exception. Reason: the @WebMvcTest slice loads no JPA, so the real repository does not fit, and OwnerRepository inherits the full JpaRepository surface, which makes a hand-written double disproportionate. Stub findById with a real Owner -> Pet -> Visit graph whose visit carries an id. Observe 'exactly one visit, corrected' on the Owner captured from save. Observe 'unchanged' and 'refused' as save never invoked.

patterns.description: optional path variable on a shared @ModelAttribute method distinguishes create from edit
resolve-by-identity lookup to mirror on Pet for its visits
existing refusal of an unowned pet by IllegalArgumentException; reuse for an unowned visit

risks.risk: The shared model-attribute method attaches a new blank Visit to the pet on every request, so an edit route that reaches it unchanged persists a second visit through the cascade (or fails @NotBlank at flush).
risks.mitigation: Branch on the optional visitId before creating a Visit (system-design.md § Contracts invariant: a visit is corrected in place, resolved through owner and pet). The 'exactly one visit' test pins it.

risks.risk: Binding onto a persisted entity could mutate stored state on a failed validation.
risks.mitigation: open-in-view is disabled (system-design.md § Persistence), so the resolved graph is detached. Without a save call nothing is written. The failure path must return before owners.save.

risks.risk: Path: resolving one visit by identity within a pet scales with that pet's visit count.
risks.mitigation: system-design.md § Scale and Load row 'One pet's visits': linear scan of the eagerly loaded set, the simplest readable form.

risks.risk: Re-adding the non-future-date check inside the new handler would add a business rule to a controller.
risks.mitigation: Rule lives on Visit and both handlers delegate (architecture-principles.md Web controller row and checklist).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. Design docs written this dispatch: docs/system-design.md adds REQ-VIS-003 to the Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController Contracts rows and adds a correct-in-place invariant sentence. It updates two Threat Model mitigations (visit binder allow-list; Visit decides the non-future date) and adds § Scale and Load from the doctor template, carrying the one row this slice needs. docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for the 2026-09-18 non-goal ADR, as the prd-entry requested. No new ADR: the change applies existing principles and has no new trade-off. Doctor check green. Template decision within REQ-LANG-002, narrowest reading: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html stays unchanged. Its heading already drops 'New' for a persisted visit, and the form posts to its own URL. The submit button still reads 'Add Visit' in correction mode. A distinct label needs a new message key translated into all eleven bundles, so it is recorded as an open question for the owner rather than done here. Brief follow-up outside this agent's write scope: architecture-principles.md line 91 lists the non-future-visit-date check among the controller-held rules. Once this slice lands, Visit makes that decision, so the brief's owner should narrow that sentence. The PRD open question on correcting past visits to a past date is unaffected. The narrow reading (booking rule) is what the Visit query implements. Uncommitted docs/adr edits from the product expert (the new non-goal ADR and the 2026-08-08 status line) are theirs, as their prd-entry notes list.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Ownership chain holds on the new edit routes: loadPetWithVisit re-resolves owner by path id, pet via owner.getPet(petId) (VisitController.java:73 `Pet pet = owner.getPet(petId);`), and the visit via pet.getVisit(visitId), which only matches persisted visits in that pet's collection (Pet.java `if (!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id))`). A visit id belonging to another pet is refused before binding on both GET and POST, and a test covers this (VisitControllerTests.java:205 `void theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAVisitNotBelongingToThePet(HttpMethod method)`). Nothing is trusted across requests (security-principles.md, cross-request state row).

Mass assignment is tighter than before: the class-level @InitBinder now adds `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");` next to the id disallow-list. Because the binder has no name qualifier, it also covers the `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` parameter on both POST handlers. Before this change, that parameter could bind Owner contact fields from the request and persist them through owners.save(owner), for example the `.param("name", "George")` the existing new-visit tests send. That pre-existing path is now closed.
Validation is the same on both persisting paths: processUpdateVisitForm takes `@Valid Visit visit` and applies the same Visit.isDateOnOrBefore(today) rejection as booking before owners.save(owner).

The new exception message (`"Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + pet.getId()`) carries only two integer identifiers taken from the path. It adds no credential or internal detail to the error page, which renders exception messages. It follows the same pattern as the existing owner and pet not-found messages at VisitController.java:70-76.

Output escaping unchanged: the shared template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders user-derived values only through th:text and the inputField fragment, with no th:utext and no Thymeleaf preprocessing (`__${...}__`). The form has no th:action, so the edit route posts back to its own URL. The hidden `petId` input falls outside the allow-list and is not bound.

New surface stated: GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit adds no mutation beyond what the open new-visit POST already allows, under the documented demonstration baseline with no auth and no CSRF (system-design.md Security Context). Management exposure is unchanged.

Supply chain and secrets: the change set touches no build file (`git diff --stat -- build.gradle pom.xml` printed nothing), so no dependency changed. A grep of the added lines for password|secret|token|apikey|credential found no hits. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (no match in build.gradle), so no NVD match ran. `./gradlew dependencies` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1 and jackson-databind 3.1.5.

But it changes behavior on a route the slice does not name, and the design-block's three-part plan does not include it. The rest reads as expected: the isDateOnOrBefore refactor keeps the null and today boundary exactly, getVisit skips unsaved visits, and a foreign visitId throws before binding.
